title: Ferromagnetic Bloch Line as a Bead on a String
abstract: We present a simple model of a Bloch line in a thin-film ferromagnet with strong easy-axis and intermediate in-plane anisotropies. The meron is represented as a charged, massless particle that slides along the linear domain wall in a background magnetic field- a gyroscopic bead on a string. Its gyroscopic behavior dynamically isolates the wall segments on either side of the meron, motivating the model for a Bloch line as two strings joined at a moving boundary. The meron clamps the wall at this junction, completely reflecting low-amplitude spin waves that propagate along it. Out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields and spin-transfer torques then act in two ways: by exerting a force on the Bloch line itself, or by driving the wall as a whole. Predictions of this model are in agreement with numerical simulations.
summary: This paper develops a mechanical model treating a magnetic Bloch line as a meron bead constrained between two domain wall segments. It derives the equations of motion, showing that the meron clamps the wall and its dynamics are dictated by external magnetic fields. The theory is validated by comparing predictions against detailed micromagnetic simulations.
main_problem: The paper aims to understand the complex dynamics of a Bloch line (a magnetic soliton) within a ferromagnetic thin film.
main_result: The meron acts as a dynamic clamp on the domain wall, reflecting low-amplitude spin waves, and its motion is governed by forces derived from external magnetic fields and internal tensions.
method: The dynamics are modeled by treating the system as a charged particle (meron) constrained between two elastic 'strings' (domain wall segments), leading to a reduced Lagrangian and equations of motion.
model_or_system: The physical system is a ferromagnetic thin film containing a Bloch line. The model simplifies this by representing the meron as a bead sliding along the domain wall, which is conceptually split into two interacting strings.
key_observables: Meron velocity ($\dot{\mathbf{r}}_m$), spin wave dispersion relation ($\omega^2 = c^2k^2 \sqrt{1 + k^2\lambda_m^2}$), and the force exerted by external fields ($B_z, B_x$).
important_parameters: Tension ($\sigma$), mass density ($ho$), gyroscopic constant ($G$), and topological charges ($\zeta_w, \zeta_m, \zeta_c$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes strong easy-axis and intermediate in-plane anisotropies, and utilizes approximations like separating length scales ($\lambda_w \ll \lambda_m \ll l$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual model of the meron on a domain wall as a bead on a string, and show comparisons between theoretical predictions and MuMax3 micromagnetic simulations under applied fields.
paper_structure: The paper builds from a conceptual model (bead on a string) to deriving a reduced Lagrangian, analyzing the equations of motion under external fields ($B_z, B_x$), and finally validating the theory against detailed micromagnetic simulations.
why_interesting: The use of mechanical analogies (bead on a string) to describe complex topological magnetic dynamics is highly relevant for understanding emergent collective excitations in condensed matter systems, bridging continuum mechanics with magnetism.

FIG. 2. Meron on a domain wall at the intersection of two circles with exaggerated curvature. The circles are free to move up or down in order to keep the meron at the point of intersection as it travels across the film.

FIG. 3. Piece-wise animation of the domain wall and meron according to our theory in a 20 mT magnetic field at a film length of 375 nm. The turning points used here are displaced from the core - a phenomenological correction to reconcile the meron’s internal structure with our point-particle description. The red kink denotes the fast side and the blue represents the high tension slow side. At the moment the field is turned on, the meron will travel into the high-tension region, reducing the overall Zeeman energy.
